question.text: In a trust-structured Category I/II AIF, the Net Asset Value (NAV) represents:

answer.text: The value of the unit capital / beneficial interest based on the periodic valuation of the fund's underlying portfolio
The amount invested by the sponsor
The total expenses of the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines NAV as the value of unit capital / beneficial interest derived from the fund's underlying portfolio valuation, disclosed periodically to investors. For Category I and II AIFs, the workbook requires independent valuation of investments at least once every six months, which can be extended to once a year with approval of at least 75 percent of investors. Valuation of illiquid and unlisted investments necessarily involves estimates, so NAV is the periodic, valuation-based per-unit value of the fund. The Trap: Management fees, sponsor commitment, and aggregate expenses are inputs to or deductions from the fund's books — they are not, individually, the NAV. Note: The Series XIX-A frequency wording was corrected: Category I/II AIF valuations are required at least every six months, extendable to once a year with 75 percent investor approval, and may involve estimates for illiquid/unlisted investments. The earlier "quarterly or semi-annually" generalisation, Cross-Exam, and Pro-Tip paragraphs were removed.
